sections.title: The Temptation of Jesus
observations: In this section, we see Jesus being led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. This highlights the reality of spiritual warfare and the importance of relying on God's Word in times of trial.

The three temptations presented to Jesus correspond to the three areas of temptation that John speaks of in 1 John 2:16: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life. Jesus' responses demonstrate His complete reliance on Scripture and His commitment to God's will.

sections.title: Jesus Begins His Ministry
observations: After overcoming temptation, Jesus begins His public ministry in Galilee. This marks a significant transition from His private life to His role as the Messiah.
The calling of His first disciples, Simon Peter and Andrew, illustrates the immediate response required to follow Christ. Their willingness to leave their nets signifies the cost of discipleship.

sections.title: Jesus Heals the Sick
observations: This section emphasizes the compassion of Jesus as He heals various diseases and afflictions. It serves as a demonstration of His authority and the fulfillment of prophecy regarding the Messiah.
The crowds that follow Him indicate the growing recognition of His power and the hope He brings to those in need.

importantVerses.commentary: Jesus responds to the devil's temptation by quoting Scripture, emphasizing the importance of spiritual nourishment over physical needs.
Jesus commands Satan to worship the Lord only, highlighting the exclusivity of worship due to God alone.
Jesus calls His disciples to be 'fishers of men,' illustrating the mission of the church to reach others with the Gospel.

questions: What can we learn from Jesus' responses to temptation about handling our own temptations?
How does the calling of the disciples reflect the nature of true discipleship?
In what ways does Jesus' healing ministry reveal His character and mission?
